deck_title: Stokes-Einstein D = k_B*T / (6*pi*mu*a) Brownian diffusivity & MSD law vs naive viscosity-invariant white-noise jitter rig

cards.subtitle: Deterministic Albert Einstein (1905), William Sutherland (1905), and Marian Smoluchowski (1906) Brownian motion fluctuation-dissipation law (dividing Boltzmann thermal energy k_B * T by Stokes viscous drag zeta = 6 * pi * mu * a so diffusivity D = k_B * T / (6 * pi * mu * a) = D_0 / (1 + u) and mean-squared displacement <|Delta r|^2> = 6 * D * t, locking D_active / D_Einstein = 1.0000x across all 17 Stokes-drag stations u = (mu*a)/(mu_0*a_0) - 1 in [0.000, 1.000] with 0/17 violated) versus naive viscosity-invariant white-noise jitter shader (D = D_0, which overestimates Brownian MSD by (mu*a)/(mu_0*a_0) = 1 + u to 1.2500x at S4, 1.5000x at S8, and 2.0000x at S16 across 16/17 stations) and 64-lag Green-Kubo Langevin velocity autocorrelation quadrature.

cards.headline: Exact controls are useful; realism remains a separate job.
good_fit: 3D Tyndall sunbeam dust motes, cellular cytoplasm nanoparticle diffusion, colloidal suspension animations, and Euler-Maruyama Langevin particle solvers
Scaling per-step Gaussian random displacement standard deviation as sigma_step = sqrt(2 * D * dt) = sqrt(k_B * T * dt / (3 * pi * mu * a))
Enforcing physical size and viscosity sorting where larger particles and thicker fluids jitter more slowly
not_for: Macroscopic boulders or planets where thermal k_B*T energy is negligible
Ballistic vacuum trajectories with zero thermal bath
